headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: cognee handles personal/finance data while the course agent writes files, runs shells, and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents and support data, while production-agentic-rag-course reads/writes local files and exposes stdin/stdout and API surfaces. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if A’s outputs are fed into B’s prompts or notebooks. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or notebooks without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace or file handoff path, attacker-controlled content can steer B.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around A outputs before B consumes them.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files in B.
Review one sample A→B handoff for instruction-like text.
Use a read-only staging file for A outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, and agent_b handles configuration secrets while reading/writing files and running shells in a local development environment. If they share a workspace or B ingests A’s documents, sensitive data can be exposed or exfiltrated through B’s allowlisted network egress. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles alone, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_a data is placed in any directory readable by agent_b, leakage is possible.
IF agent_b processes files containing personal or finance data, those contents may reach its inference/API calls.
IF B’s allowlisted egress includes external services, copied secrets can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Remove sensitive files from B’s working tree.
Rotate any secrets exposed to B.
Run B with a dummy dataset for validation.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances with session memory, and agent_b supports multiple instances with local filesystem writes and shell execution. Overlapping mutable access can conflict if both operate on the same workspace, even though B does not modify git state. The profiles do not prove shared locking, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF multiple instances of either agent run against one workspace, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Check for existing output files before writing.
Use immutable inputs for A.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while agent_b exposes agentic ask and stream endpoints that can turn upstream text into downstream actions or generated content. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect writing or retrieval results. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A’s outputs as source material without verification, mistakes propagate.
IF A’s decisions are fed into B’s agentic endpoints, downstream actions may reflect errors.
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A outputs.
Add a citation/grounding check for A-derived claims.
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking, for A inputs.
Spot-check one end-to-end example.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment with external API keys. If EU or regulated data from A is routed into B’s course environment or third-party services, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not state a DPA or residency boundary, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data from A enters B’s environment, compliance review is required.
IF B forwards that data to external APIs, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B’s inputs.
Confirm a DPA before any external transfer.
Document retention for B’s logs and notebooks.
Purge test artifacts after review.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing controls.
